**Job Description

**_Transaction Banking is changing fast, and the way customers connect with their bank is becoming more sophisticated. Danske Bank is bringing its Customer Implementation and Integration areas together under one unit, and we are looking for a leader who can create a shared direction, build a strong leadership team, and make complex customer journeys simpler and more consistent across five markets.

_**What You Will Be Doing

**You will lead a newly unified organisation spanning Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Lithuania, bringing together experienced leaders, specialist teams and distinct capabilities. Reporting directly to the Head of TxB Sales Enablement, you will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Product, Technology, IT and Tribe organisations to shape end-to-end customer experiences. Your role sits at the intersection of business, operations and technology, and the decisions you make will shape how corporate customers and financial institutions connect with Danske Bank.

More specifically, you will:

• Set the strategic direction and priorities across all five markets

• Build and develop a leadership team grounded in clarity, empowerment and accountability

• Connect Customer Implementation and Integration to create more seamless customer journeys

• Partner with IT and Tribe teams to shape customer-facing solutions and internal tooling

• Use client insights to inform implementation journeys, integration solutions and commercial priorities

• Encourage the responsible adoption of AI to simplify processes and build employee capabilities

**About You

**

• Solid experience leading organisations through other leaders

• Genuine commitment to developing people, teams and leadership cultures

• Ability to create direction across countries or complex organisational structures

• Skilled at translating strategy into clear priorities and tangible outcomes

• Strong customer and commercial orientation

• Comfortable at the intersection of business, operations and technology

• Able to bring structure and clarity to ambiguous, multi-stakeholder situations

You do not need to come from a traditional banking background. Experience from financial services, consulting, technology, transformation, customer implementation, integrations, APIs, cash management or similar environments is equally relevant and welcome.

**What We Offer You

**This is a rare opportunity to shape a newly formed organisation and leave a lasting mark on how Danske Bank delivers for its customers. You will work in a hybrid model, typically three to four days per week in the office, alongside talented colleagues across multiple markets. We invest in our leaders and offer genuine scope to grow, both in the role and across the wider organisation.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**If this sounds like the right move for you, we encourage you to apply. You are also welcome to reach out to Natasha Rajovic, Head of TxB Sales Enablement, at nkuz@danskebank.dk with any questions before applying.

Location: Aarhus or Copenhagen.

**We look forward to hearing from you!

****About Us

**Danske Bank is a Nordic bank with bridges to the world around us. For 150 years, we have supported people and businesses in releasing their potential. A career with us is an opportunity to join a community of 22,000 colleagues in a culture where we are committed to Teaming Up, Owning It and Being Open. Together, we are on a journey to transform Danske Bank into a better bank. For our customers, our employees and the societies around us.

**Job Description

**_Are you studying Data Technician and want to work with IT support and operations, Linux, Windows, Oracle, Azure, or VmWare? We are seeking talented apprentices for Netcompany Operations with 1-2 years remaining in your education, who want to apply their technical knowledge in practice.

_**Responsibilities & Technologies

**Netcompany Operations is an established operations organization that handles everything from business and societally critical application operations to infrastructure management in modern data centers and in public cloud.

Our customer base is highly diverse, ranging from small private companies to large public-sector projects. We are not interested in operations for operations' sake, but work with operations based on a vision of making a difference for our customers' business. Regardless of the projects and tasks size, you, as an apprentice in Netcompany Operations, will make a noticeable difference.

As an Operations apprentice, you will join one of our many teams on equal footing with your colleagues. You will work with Linux, Windows, Oracle, Azure, or VmWare tasks, which cover everything from handling alarms and system errors to implementing changes across solutions. Your tasks may also include maintaining documentation, reporting, operations, and more. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to participate in projects from start to finish, which will give you insight into the entire process.

**Your Responsibilites Will Typically Include

**

• Incident management: Handling errors reported by systems as well as customers.

• Change management: Handling both standard changes and project-ordered changes.

• Quality initiatives: Handling measures across solutions to help deliver, ensure, and improve quality.

• Windows and Linux server operations.

• Maintenance of documentation, reporting, deploys, and similar.

**About You

**We believe that you are initiative-taking, eager to learn new things, and dream of an apprenticeship where you can be challenged by putting your technical knowledge into practice. In addition, we are looking for a person who is motivated, works independently and analytically minded.

**To Succeed In This Role, You

**

• Are studying Data Technician with a specialization in infrastructure or programming, preferably combined with a EUX, and have completed foundation modules 1 and 2.

• Are eager to learn new things.

• Have experience with either Networks, Linux, Windows, Oracle, Azure, or VmWare (not a requirement).

• Have experience from previous apprenticeships on a shorter or longer basis (not a requirement.)

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Your background, qualifications, and interests are important to us to ensure you have the best apprenticeship.

**Continue developing with us

**At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

**Join an inclusive community

**At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

**Send us your application

**Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

_All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

_We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance.

Inpay is hiring a Senior Risk Officer, in a senior role reporting directly to the Chief Risk Officer, to be the right hand of the CRO: the person who owns our senior stakeholder relationships on risk, builds our AI framework for risk, and runs business-wide risk assessments that leadership can act on. You bring 7 to 9 years of hands-on, banking-grade risk experience, work autonomously, and make the call when it matters. What you will do

**At GN, we are bringing people closer, and through our Jabra brand, we are leading major technology shifts with intelligent audio solutions.

**We are looking for an Audio DSP Test Engineer to join our Audio DSP team and help develop, maintain, and improve our audio test systems for audio platforms used in Jabra headsets, earbuds, and accessories.

The position is based in our HQ in Ballerup, where we have our test setup.

You will join 20 highly skilled and dedicated colleagues. We are organised in agile teams, each with a maximum of 8 developers, 1 Scrum Master, and 1 Product Owner. You will report to the Line Manager, audio DSP ESW, while your daily work will be carried out closely with your team and the projects you are allocated to.

**What will you be doing?

**As an Audio DSP Test Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality and robustness of our Audio DSP software through automated hardware testing, software testing of DSP code, and audio validation based on a DSP.

You will work with our automatic HW test system, developing and maintaining test frameworks, test cases, tools, and infrastructure used to validate audio DSP features on real target hardware.

**Your Work Will Include

**

• Providing insights into test strategy and best practices

• Developing, maintaining, and improving automated HW test systems for Audio DSP platforms

• Designing and implementing automated test cases for audio features and DSP algorithms

• Integrating test solutions with embedded software builds and continuous integration workflows

• Debugging failures across test software, embedded DSP software, hardware, and test equipment

• Analysing test results, identifying root causes, and collaborating with developers to resolve issues

• Supporting validation of audio performance, stability, interfaces, and system behaviour on target hardware

• Improving test coverage, test reliability, execution time, and reporting

• Documenting test setups, test methods, and results

**Sound good so far? Here’s what you’ll need to succeed:

**

• You have a degree in electrical engineering, computer science, software engineering, or similar

• You have experience with embedded software testing, test automation, or hardware-in-the-loop testing

• You have experience scripting and test tooling in Python, and preferably developing software in C/C++

• You have experience with embedded debugging and analysing issues across hardware and software

• You have an interest in audio DSP software, audio processing, and validation of audio features

• You understand fixed- and floating-point signal processing, or are motivated to build expertise in this area

• You are comfortable working systematically with test design, automation, troubleshooting, and data analysis

Experience with Bluetooth chipsets, such as Airoha, Qualcomm, or other platforms using Tensilica HiFi cores, is an advantage.

**A keen interest in relevant technologies and methods

**You do not need to be an expert in every aspect of automated testing or audio DSP from day one. However, curiosity, a structured mindset, and motivation to learn new technologies and methods will take you far at GN.

We work with DSP, embedded development, DSP architectures, interfaces such as I2S/TDM, C/C++, Python, Git, code review tools, automated test frameworks, and laboratory test equipment.

**Team-player spirit

**While there are plenty of opportunities for each team member to develop their individual skill set, we are first and foremost a team.

**Fluent Written And Spoken English Skills

**Our official company language is English.

**The GN Audio culture

**The GN Audio culture is upbeat and positive. We greet every day with energy and enthusiasm and approach problem-solving and challenges with a “glass half full” attitude.

We are a multicultural team with colleagues in several countries. The team is a mix of local and remote colleagues, and online collaboration is part of our DNA.

**Think you’ve got what it takes? Apply now.

**To apply, use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than Dec 4, 2026. Applications are assessed on a continuous basis, and we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

If you want to learn more about the position, you are welcome to contact the Audio DSP Manager, Martin R Andersen, mrandersen@gn.group

Are you an experienced and hands-on People Operations professional who enjoys being at the heart of a busy People function? Do you perform well in a busy environment where attention to detail, service, and productivity are key?

At TORM, our corporate functions work closely with our shipping organization to support the business forward. Through our One TORM approach, our commercial, technical and support functions work as one integrated organization.

As our People Operations Manager, you will become a key part of our People team in Denmark, based at our office in Hellerup, Tuborg Havn.

Your Role: Contribute to the Team

Reporting to the Head of People, you will be part of our international People team working across Denmark and our other global locations.

You will be responsible for People Operations and payroll activities, primarily supporting our Denmark-based employees and managers. Working closely with our People Business Partners and colleagues across locations, you will ensure high-quality People services while continuously improving our processes, systems and employee experience.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Backup for the monthly payroll process for Denmark, ensuring accurate and timely payroll execution in close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders

• Manage employment contracts, addenda, letters and other People-related documentation and templates

• Manage employee onboarding and offboarding processes

• Manage the evaluation, improvement and optimization of People workflows and processes

• Coordinate practical and administrative matters related to secondments and relocations

• Guide managers and employees on employment legislation, tax-related matters and People policies

• Administer parental leave and sick leave, including reimbursement applications

• Maintain employee handbooks, policies and other People documentation

Your Profile

We are looking for an experienced People Operations professional who combines solid HR knowledge with a practical and service-minded approach. You enjoy working with people, systems and processes, and you take pride in delivering accurate work while keeping things moving.

To do well in this role, you bring:

• A solid understanding of Danish payroll and experience working with payroll processes

• Good knowledge of HR/People systems, processes and employee data, we use CatalystOne

• Knowledge of Danish employment legislation, including the Danish Salaried Employees Act and Holiday Act

• Proficiency using Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Excel, Word and PowerPoint

• Fluent Danish and English, both written and spoken

• A collaborative mindset and a sense of ownership

You are a problem solver who follows through on commitments and can manage several competing priorities without compromising quality. Just as importantly, you enjoy contributing to an energetic, informal and positive working environment.

What We Offer

At TORM, we are committed to people, communities and the environment. We offer a competitive salary reflecting your experience and qualifications, together with an attractive benefits package including bonus, pension and health insurance.

Our flexible working arrangements provide additional flexibility in balancing professional and personal commitments.

You will also become part of an international and informal working environment with opportunities to learn, develop and collaborate across our global organization.

Our employee activities and associations provide plenty of opportunities to connect with colleagues beyond your day-to-day work.

At TORM, diversity and inclusion are integral to our performance. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and value the different perspectives and experiences they bring.

How to Apply

Interested to join the People team? Submit your application and CV via www.torm.com/careers by 27 November 2026. Applications will be reviewed continuously.

For more information about the position, please contact Head of People, Lene Stampe Sørensen, +45 2428 8270.

We look forward to hearing from you!

We are looking for a Software Engineer who wants to build and ship new features that quickly reach customers, on top of an engine that already runs at scale. You join our platform team, which owns several live domains that our customers depend on every day. The foundations are solid and well maintained, so your time goes into new use cases and features rather than firefighting. Whether you have a couple of years of experience or a few more, we would like to see your application.

**What's in it for you?

**

• Hear directly from the people using what you build. Customer feedback feeds straight back into the roadmap, and you work on features and product decisions that matter to end users.

• Build on a system with real scale behind it. The event system spans 8 domains, exposes 20+ event types as webhooks, and powers 10 configurable alert types for our end users - currently ~20k active configurations triggering ~200k events every weekday. The team owns 8+ public APIs end to end, crucial for customers' day-to-day business.

• Learn from experts who share. You’ll join a talkative team of experienced domain experts who love discussing technical topics.

• Grow with support. Scoped, well-defined assignments to start, senior colleagues pairing and reviewing your work, and shared ownership of keeping things running.

• See your work ship. We favour small, frequent releases over long project cycles, so what you build lands in production fast.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend developer with strong Java skills who is at home on live production systems.

• Hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, and REST APIs, in particular building and running your own services in a modern cloud-based microservice and event-driven architecture.

• You are comfortable working on live production systems with high data volumes and migration paths, keeping quality, observability, reliability, and performance in mind.

• You enjoy talking tech: you like discussing technical topics widely, learning, and listening in on topics not always directly related to your own tasks.

• You are motivated by incremental, high-quality delivery on products that are already live, bringing a fresh perspective that helps rework existing infrastructure where it is holding us back, and you treat the tools already in our platform as solid building blocks.

• Nice to have: Flink and stateful processing (or the willingness to learn it, since it is widely used here), relational databases, and Grafana and Prometheus, our “bread and butter”.

You embrace AI as part of how you engineer. From prototyping through to production, you use AI tools as an integrated part of your workflow, not as a shortcut but as a force multiplier. That said, this isn't the main thing we're hiring for: curiosity and a willingness to use it well matter more than deep prior experience.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Improve, extend and run the live domains our team owns, including telemetry storage and APIs, the event system, and the alerting engine, without disrupting production.

• Build and run your own services, with migration paths when architecture or data formats need to change.

• Work closely with the internal teams building products on top of the platform you help shape.

• Keep the platform reliable and observable at high data volumes.

****Our hiring process

****Don’t waste your time writing the perfect cover letter. We want you to create an impact that matters - and that’s not in the cover letter.

• Initial phone conversation with a colleague from our P&T team.

• Virtual meet and greet with your potential new leader and someone from the team, so you’ll get to know the role and team better.

• Assignment-specific interview with the hiring manager and a lead engineer from the team. We want to give you a real insight into the work. You’ll receive a case to prepare ahead of the interview and present to relevant colleagues - people you’ll also work closely with in the role.

• If needed, we will obtain references from former employers and conduct background checks at relevant levels.

• Offer presentation and walk-through.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We’re committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products - it’s a way of life at Trackunit. We’re proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues come together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

jobs.occupation: PhD Position at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) Religious Education, Legal Consciousness and Social Cohesion in Post-Imperial Islamic Societies
jobs.description:
The Department of Law at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded three-year PhD position within the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network MINARET – Islamic Legal Cultures in Post-Imperial Contexts. Employment is expected to begin September 1, 2027, or by agreement.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences and employed at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark.

 

About the MINARET Doctoral Network

MINARET is an international doctoral network funded through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA). The network investigates how Islamic legal cultures shape governance, citizenship, institutions and everyday legal practices across post-imperial societies.

The programme brings together universities and non-academic partners across Europe, North Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia. Doctoral candidates will receive interdisciplinary training, international supervision and extensive mobility opportunities.

Further information about the network is available at MINARET website.

 

Project Description

This doctoral project examines how constitutional and legal frameworks governing religious education shape citizenship, legal consciousness and social cohesion in Indonesia and Morocco.

The project investigates how constitutional values, religious identities and civic norms are translated into educational practices and everyday experiences of citizenship. Particular attention is paid to how religious education influences democratic participation, social integration and perceptions of rights, duties and belonging.

The project contributes to research on legal consciousness, sociology of law, citizenship studies and comparative constitutionalism. Through comparative empirical research in Indonesia and Morocco, the doctoral candidate will analyse how educational institutions function as sites where legal norms, religious values and civic identities intersect.

The candidate is expected to develop an original research design within the overall framework of the project.

 

Host Institution

The position is based at the Department of Law, University of Southern Denmark, Denmark.

The Department of Law is part of the Faculty of Social Sciences and hosts a vibrant interdisciplinary environment within sociology of law, legal anthropology, human rights and comparative legal studies.

The successful candidate will become part of the department’s research environment as well as the international MINARET doctoral network.

More information about our PhD programme is available at the department’s website. On the website, you will also find the department’s qualifications criteria. The programme is provided by the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences who offer further information on their website.

 

Supervision

The doctoral candidate will be supervised by:

• 
Professor Ole Hammerslev (University of Southern Denmark) (principal supervisor)

• 
Co-supervisor from MINARET consortium

Additional mentoring and supervision will be provided through the MINARET network.

 

Fieldwork and Mobility

The project includes substantial international mobility.

The doctoral candidate is expected to conduct fieldwork in:

• 
Indonesia

• 
Morocco

 

In addition, the candidate will undertake two secondments within the MINARET network:

• 
one academic secondment at a partner university;

• 
one non-academic secondment with a relevant partner organisation.

 

Participation in network-wide training events, workshops, summer schools and conferences is mandatory.

 

Tasks and Responsibilities

The successful candidate will:

• 
conduct independent doctoral research within the project framework;

• 
participate actively in the MINARET doctoral network;

• 
undertake international fieldwork and secondments;

• 
complete PhD courses and training activities;

• 
contribute to the research environment at the Department of Law;

• 
participate in teaching and related activities in accordance with Danish PhD regulations.

 

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree (or equivalent) in law, sociology, political science, anthropology, religious studies, education, or a related social science discipline.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements of the PhD School at SDU Business School and the Faculty of Social Sciences, SDU, which you can learn more about on the PhD School’s website. 

Applicants must also meet requirements in accordance with the MSCA Doctoral Network:

• 
applicants must not already hold a doctoral degree;

• 
applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.

Excellent English language skills are required.

 

Desired Qualifications

Preference will be given to applicants with documented experience or interest in one or more of the following areas:

• 
sociology of law;

• 
legal consciousness;

• 
citizenship studies;

• 
religion and law;

• 
Islamic legal cultures;

• 
qualitative and comparative research methods;

• 
fieldwork-based research.

 

Knowledge of Arabic, Bahasa Indonesia, French or other relevant languages is an advantage but not a requirement.

 

Assessment Criteria

Applicants will be assessed on:

• 
academic qualifications (please consult the guidelines for recognizing merit at the Department of Law);

• 
quality and feasibility of the proposed research project;

• 
methodological competencies;

• 
motivation and suitability for international and interdisciplinary research;

• 
ability to contribute to the objectives of the MINARET doctoral network.

 

We Offer

The position offers:

• 
Three years of full-time employment as a PhD fellow at SDU;

• 
enrolment in an internationally recognised PhD programme;

• 
participation in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network;

• 
international supervision and training;

• 
research mobility and secondments;

• 
competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with Danish regulations and MSCA provisions.

 

Contact information

For more information about the department and the position, please contact Head of Department, Ole Hammerslev, ohv@sam.sdu.dk. 

 

Terms of employment      
The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) for academics in the state sector, including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at universities and the regulations for PhD students as described therein.

Employment as a PhD student is subject to the circular of 20 December 2021, on the agreement for academics in the state sector – Appendix 5, protocol on PhD students.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

 

The assessment and evaluation process

Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material.

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. 

 

Application   

 

The application must include the following:

•   Motivated application
•   Detailed Curriculum vitae (educational and work history should be specified by month and year)
•   A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results – alternatively, the expected date to finish the master’s degree. Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used. 
•   An application form (is available here)
•   A project description (max 5 pages of 2,400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.). The guidelines for preparing a PhD project proposal for the Department of Law are available here.
•   An abstract of the project description of no more than 250 words
•   Publications, if any – however, no more than two. If one of the attached publications is a master thesis, only the problem formulation and the conclusion should be attached, not the entire thesis.
•   Information on teaching experience or other forms of academic communication.

Documents which are not in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish must be translated into English. SDU may discard applications which are incomplete regarding the above-mentioned criteria without further notice. All documents must be in pdf format, no more than 5 MB per file. 

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. If you experience technical problems when uploading the application, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

UPLOAD GUIDE: Motivated application should be uploaded as ‘Cover letter’, Curriculum Vitae should be uploaded as ‘Resume’. All other documents should be uploaded as ‘Miscellaneous documents’. 

 

The application deadline is January 31, 2027, 23.59 CET/CEST.

 Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

 

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

**The Opportunity

**Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. As the most senior engineer on the team, you will own the technical direction of the platform security, identity, and network security slice, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across platform security, identity, and network security, and rolling out the first paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, CVE response, CI/CD identity, and a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen). You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers write, review and ship secure systems.

**What You Will Do

**You will join a focused platform security team and operate as its most senior engineer. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities, and we expect this role to set the bar.

• Design and build the paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, and CVE response, running inside the pipelines teams already use, with findings routed to the owners who can fix them under tracked SLAs

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for a unified internal network and VPN across GCP, AWS, and our Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen offices, while the team that owns the network keeps running it

• Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own

• Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves

• Build audit logging as a shared capability that teams plug into rather than reinvent

• Turn GRC controls into technical implementations, with evidence pipelines that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Own the contracting cycle for external penetration tests and build the intake, classification, and tracking system that routes findings to named owners, while the owning teams remediate

• Hand each capability off cleanly, with a runbook, a named owner, and an escalation path, and run office hours where product and platform teams can get a security review or a paved-road question answered

• Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

**What You Could Bring

**This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

• Platform security: you have run vulnerability scanning, CVE management, and image scanning at scale, and you know the operational reality of getting CVEs fixed, beyond standing up the tooling

• Identity and auth: you have worked hands-on inside an auth codebase, rolled out MFA on live systems, and managed token lifecycles in CI/CD with OIDC and workload identity

• Network security at scale: you have designed and run a unified internal network across multiple cloud providers and offices, with a VPN approach that holds up

• Platform-as-product mindset: you have built internal security tooling that other teams chose to adopt, with guard rails built into the tools developers already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured the impact

• Infrastructure as Code: strong experience with Terraform, Crossplane, or similar

Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

**How We Work

**You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. This role sets the technical direction for the team's quarterly missions. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on three or four items but not all of them, apply anyway. The "deep in one, ready to grow into the other" framing above is not a hedge, it is how we actually hire at this level. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

**About The Role

**We sell electricity data through an API: carbon intensity, power prices and grid forecasts. Tech companies use it to report and minimize emissions. Wind and solar producers and grid-scale battery solutions use it to predict prices and plan their market participation. EV companies use it to build smart-charging features. CS is about ensuring every one of these customers actually uses the data to do their job better, stays with us and grows with us.

You’ll build out Customer Success at Electricity Maps. That means onboarding new customers, running renewals and spotting where an account could grow, while trialling and defining the processes and tooling that make it all repeatable. You'll work closely with Sales, Product and our Data team. This is a hands-on role: you'll own your own book of customers and a retention target.

**What You'll Do

**

• Own the end-to-end customer journey. Onboarding, product value, retention, expansion. Your job is to make sure our data delivers real value to each customer, and you’ll be measured on their retention and growth (Net Revenue Retention).

• Get new customers to value fast. Take the handoff from Sales, set expectations, and help customers get set up using the API. Find ways to hone our customer onboarding to create a smoother, better process.

• Own renewals and growth. Run renewal processes end-to-end, from positioning and proposal through signature. Proactively identify and close expansion: new zones, new data types or use cases, other teams in the same company.

• Go beyond the technical contact. Build relationships across each customer’s organization, branching out past technical contacts to understand and align with the business outcomes the data supports. Build executive relationships with strategic accounts, and run periodic business reviews that tie our data to their goals.

• Manage a mixed book. Your accounts will range from high-profile logos to smaller customers, with deal sizes to match. You’ll juggle competing priorities, keep an eye on the details, and find the right way to serve each account, so every customer gets real value and results for them and for Electricity Maps.

• Build the low-touch motion. Design the onboarding, check-in and renewal sequences that serve the long tail of customers who are smaller value and have less growth potential. In short, you’ll help us learn how best we can serve these customers at scale.

• Connect customers and product. Find out what customers are building, where they get stuck and what we could do better. Identify themes, and relay insights internally to help shape Product and Sales strategies. In return also keep customers close to our roadmap: new zones, forecast model improvements, and what’s coming.

• Build the tools you need. The tooling behind CS is yours to shape. Where there’s a gap, from health scoring and renewal alerts to onboarding flows and automated emails, you’ll build the solution yourself instead of waiting for someone else to.

****Must-haves

**

• You have 3-5 years working with customers after the sale at a B2B tech company, in Customer Success, Account Management or something similar.

• You've owned commercial conversations: renewals, upsells, pricing, pushback.

• You’ve owned a retention target, e.g. Net Revenue Retention (NRR).

• You've built something from scratch in a startup.

• You use AI tools and data to solve problems yourself. You build your own analyses, briefs and small automations.

• You can work hands-on with our technical experts one day and run a business review with a senior commercial stakeholder the next.

• You’re comfortable working with APIs and data products, and can dig into a customer’s setup to spot what’s off.

**Nice-to-haves

**

• You’ve worked at a company that sells API or data products.

• You already know the energy space: power markets, trading, grid operations and carbon emissions accounting. You can hold a conversation with an energy trader or a sustainability lead.

• You’ve been one of the first hires in a CS team and helped shape how it works, so you know what great CS looks like in practice.

**About Electricity Maps

Our data powers decisions across sustainability and energy markets: from companies like Google and Cisco optimising compute workloads and reporting emissions, to energy market participants using our forecasts to inform trading strategies and wind, solar, and battery optimisation. We're a small, technical team based in Copenhagen, working at the intersection of energy, AI, climate change, and data.

**The details

**Location: Copenhagen (in-office)

Type: Full-time

Compensation: Competitive salary + performance-based commission + pension + stock options

Benefits: 6 weeks vacation, health insurance, annual company offsite, lunch and snacks at the office.

The opportunity

Founded in 2016, Mover is a Danish logistics technology company on a mission to change logistics for good, reducing waste and making people’s lives better.

Mover is growing into new markets, and we are looking for a Business Developer to help get us there. You will own market entry projects end to end, from sourcing local contractors to go-live and handover, and negotiate the agreements that make each operation run. Compliance comes first, balanced against commercial value and speed of entry.

If that's something for you, then please read on!

Role overview and responsibilities

• Negotiate compliant, commercially sound agreements with local contractors

• Work closely with customers in your markets to understand their operations and needs, and use that insight in how we launch and run

• Keep a clear overview of requirements, deadlines and open issues in your projects, and catch errors early

• Keep CRM, pipeline and market intelligence accurate and usable for the team

Your mindset

• You are driven by purpose and want to contribute to our mission of changing logistics for good

• You are positive and curious, and see opportunities where others see constraints and barriers

• You own processes end to end and follow up without reminders

• You build solutions that work in the next market too, not only this one

• You learn on your own initiative and share knowledge with colleagues

• You are looking for a fun, friendly and ambitious working environment in a purpose-driven company where your opinion matters

What success looks like (6-12 months)

• Markets you launch go live according to plan

• Contractors are sourced within expected cost and quality parameters

• Your negotiations land agreements that are compliant and commercially sound

• Customers in your markets feel understood, and their needs shape how we operate

• You catch risks and errors before they escalate

• Improvements you implement are still in use after handover

• Local teams operate independently once you hand over

• CRM and pipeline data stay accurate and up to date

About you

• Experience from logistics, transport or supply chain

• A master's, bachelor's or other relevant education

• Experience negotiating and closing agreements with suppliers or customers

• Experience running projects with several stakeholders, deadlines and risks

• You are comfortable using data and CRM tools to guide decisions

• You have good judgement, learn fast and turn complex problems into practical solutions

What we offer

• Meaningful responsibility from day one, working alongside experienced colleagues on live projects

• A steep learning curve in a fast-moving technology company

• Autonomy, trust, and support to do the best work of your career

• An open, collaborative environment with talented peers across multiple functions

• Aaaand, a great lunch, modern offices and a cool location at Islands Brygge in the center of Copenhagen…

Lead with integrity - We believe that integrity is a reciprocal value – it means treating others as we wish to be treated. With respect, honesty, and sound ethics

Be accountable - We embrace freedom in decision-making, initiative, and actions while accepting full responsibility for outcomes and results

Push boundaries - We challenge norms, innovate, and move fast to drive changes to continuously improve things for everyone affected by our products and services

Play, as a team - We are serious without taking ourselves too seriously, and balance having fun with achieving great things, together

Note: Expect considerable travel across our markets.

Our process includes interviews, a case and a cognitive ability test. Everyone takes the test, regardless of level. It is one input among several, alongside your experience and how you solve the case.

jobs.description:
DevOps / Platform Engineer — Fully Remote, Performance & Production Ownership

Want to work fully remotely with real freedom and ownership while operating high-throughput, low-latency systems that serve billions of shoppers?

For the right person, this is a high-trust role where you have flexibility in how you structure your work and the opportunity to make a significant impact on the technology behind billions of e-commerce experiences.

We’re building the infrastructure behind better e-commerce experiences for billions of shoppers every year.

Our systems serve more than 2,000 requests per second. Our in-house search engine delivers a p50 latency of sub-ms, while our entire infrastructure maintains 99.998% uptime.

We work with modern technology, use AI as a fundamental part of how we build, and continuously push the limits of reliability, performance, and innovation. Our goal is simple: connect e-commerce shoppers with the right products at the right time while helping merchants create a better customer experience and improve their bottom line.

We’re proud of the systems we’ve built—and we want someone who is excited to help make them even faster, more reliable, and more capable.

This job will be perfect for you if

• You enjoy operating high-throughput production systems where latency, reliability, and customer impact matter

• You care deeply about reliability, latency, throughput, and system performance

• You can investigate problems across infrastructure, application code, databases, queues, and networks

• You are comfortable reading, writing, debugging, and optimising production code

• You proactively identify failure scenarios before they become incidents

• You build automation and tooling instead of accepting repetitive manual work

• You enjoy improving CI/CD, infrastructure as code, observability, and developer experience

• You have handled serious production incidents and understand the responsibility that comes with on-call

• You think beyond whether a deployment succeeded and care about how the system behaves afterwards

• You can communicate clearly during incidents and take ownership when things matter

• You are curious about new technology and enjoy finding better ways to build and operate systems

• You want to work closely with software engineers rather than treating infrastructure as a separate world

• You thrive in a remote environment where freedom is matched by responsibility

A normal day for you

No two days will be the same, but your work might include:

• Investigating why a service, query, or piece of application code is slower than it should be

• Improving the reliability and performance of systems serving thousands of requests per second

• Reviewing metrics, traces, logs, and alerts to identify issues before they affect customers

• Designing and implementing infrastructure, automation, and internal tooling

• Writing, reviewing, debugging, and optimising production code

• Working with developers to improve how systems are built, deployed, and operated

• Responding to incidents when needed, then making sure the underlying problem is permanently addressed

• Exploring how new technologies and AI-powered tools can improve our engineering workflow

• Thinking proactively about scaling, capacity, resilience, and potential failure scenarios

AI is part of the job

We’re an AI-first company. AI and agentic coding are already part of how we build, investigate, automate, and improve systems.

You should already be comfortable using AI in your daily engineering workflow—for example, to investigate incidents, generate and review code, build internal tooling, automate operational work, and improve your own productivity.

How we work

This role can be fully remote for the right person.

We believe in giving people the freedom to structure their work in a way that helps them perform at their best. We care about impact, ownership, communication, and results—not about watching when or where you work.

You’ll need to work with meaningful overlap during CET working hours and participate in our PagerDuty/on-call rotation. Freedom comes with responsibility, especially when you are responsible for production systems.

On-call includes holidays

If you are scheduled to be on call and a genuine production alarm goes off—whether that is on a normal weekday, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Eve, or New Year’s Day—you are expected to respond, take ownership, and stay with the issue until our systems are fully up and running again.

This is an important part of the role and is not optional. We are looking for someone who genuinely stands behind their work and understands that production ownership sometimes means being there when things go wrong.

At the same time, your goal is to make this situation as rare as possible. The best engineer is not the person who enjoys firefighting every holiday, but the person who builds reliable systems, strong monitoring, and effective automation so that firefighting is never needed.

How to apply

Instead of starting with a traditional cover letter, please send us a maximum 10-minute video.

We are hiring a human being—not AI-generated slop, a spotless resume, or someone who simply knows how to present the right keywords. We know the kind of person we are looking for, but the process also needs to be mutual. You should get the opportunity to meet the people behind the company and decide whether this is the right environment for you.

That is why we want to meet you upfront and see how you think, communicate, and explain your experience—not only evaluate what is written on paper.

**In The Video, Please Tell Us

**

• Who you are

• The production systems you have owned

• A difficult reliability or performance problem you solved

• What you changed and the measurable result

• How you approach incidents and on-call responsibility

• How you currently use AI and agentic coding

• Why you believe you would be a strong fit for this role

• What you are looking for in your next team and role

The video does not need to be polished. Please don’t spend time producing a perfect presentation or reading a script. We want to see the real person, understand how you think, and hear about the work you have actually done.

You may also include a short written example of a system that was slow, unreliable, or difficult to operate. Explain how you found the root cause, what you changed, and what improved afterwards.

If you are primarily an infrastructure administrator, this probably isn’t the right role. If you are a production-minded software engineer who enjoys making systems faster, more reliable, and easier to operate, we would love to hear from you.

A property manager can handle 600 tenants. That's the industry limit. Why? Because the work scales linearly: matching bank transactions to invoices, chasing late payments, answering tenant questions, coordinating repairs, preparing legal notices, renewing leases. More tenants, more of the same manual work.

With AI, that limit disappears. And both landlords and tenants get a better experience.

**About Rumli

**Eight years in property operations. ~1,000 customers across Denmark, the Netherlands, and Germany. We know this industry: the workflows, the pain points, the regulations.

Now we're making a big move: becoming a property manager. Tenant communication, bookkeeping, coordinating repairs. We handle it all. A landlord shouldn't chase late payments or find a plumber at 10 pm. We do it for them.

We're building an entirely new platform to power this. AI-native from day one. Profitable, real customers, expanding across the Nordics.

**Why this is interesting

**Property management is a great domain for a product engineer. Thousands of similar transactions, pattern-based decisions, templated documents. And 1,000 customers who will tell you exactly where it hurts. Years of domain knowledge, ready to turn into a product.

We ship with AI agents built into the workflow. Our codebase has custom skills to improve our workflow. AI writes a lot of the code; we review it. That means the slow part of building isn't writing code anymore. It's knowing what to build. That's what this role is about.

**The role

**You are autonomous and independent, working with the team to solve property managers' pains and make them as efficient as possible.

• Talk to customers and property managers. Find out what actually slows them down

• Decide what to build, then build it. Mockup, prototype, ship, measure, repeat

• Own features end-to-end. Database to API to UI

• Build AI into core product features

• Work directly with our co-founder on product direction

We need someone who looks at a messy problem and figures out what to build, and doesn't wait for a spec.

**Tech stack

**TypeScript everywhere. But does it even matter anymore?

• Frontend: Next.js, React, Shadcn, Tailwind CSS

• Backend: NestJS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM

• Infra: AWS Lambda, CDK, RDS, EventBridge, SQS

**What We're Looking For

**

• Product thinking. You understand what it takes to build a profitable product. You are not here just to handle tickets.

• Strong product mindset. Agents can code, but they need scoping and steering.

• You've shipped things people actually use, and you can show them.

• Comfortable talking to customers.

• Experience with coding agents.

• Work independently.

• Copenhagen-based (on-site).

Big plus: AWS, AI experience (prompt engineering, RAG, agents), fintech/proptech background, a side project you're proud of.

**Compensation & Benefits

**

• Compensation: 50–65K DKK, depending on experience and demonstrated competencies

• Equity: Employee warrants offering real ownership in the company

• Workspace: Centrally located Copenhagen office

• Perks: Daily lunch included

**Why Rumli?

**Real customers. Brand-new codebase. Small team where your decisions matter.

We're rebuilding from the ground up with AI as the foundation. If you want to decide what property software should do, not just build what someone else specified, reach out.
